# Claim-Source Map — `panel-npiv-discrete`

**Generated by:** Writer
**Verified by:** writer-critic
**Date:** 2026-07-31 (rebuilt in the fix round after 70/100)
**Scope:** `paper/qmd/main.qmd` §§2–4 only (Identification, Estimation, Asymptotic
properties). §1, the abstract, §5 and §7 are not yet drafted and carry no entries.

**Note on the "Source" columns.** `PROJECT_TYPE: theory`. Every quantitative claim in
§§2–4 traces to the theory corpus rather than to an estimation script, so the columns are
read as: *Source file* = the file of record; *Source line / tag* = the line number and the
`\label` of the statement that carries it. Line numbers are as of the compile-clean corpus
of 2026-07-31 16:02 (`results.tex`) / 16:09 (`proofs.tex`) / 14:22 (`assumptions.tex`).
One row is corroborated by the Monte Carlo and is marked as such; nothing in §§2–4 is
sourced *from* the simulation.

**Note on the "Location" column — the scheme changed in this round, and why.** It
previously carried `main.qmd` line numbers. Every §4 row rotted by 42–46 lines the first
time the manuscript was edited, which is the same defect class as the 77 stale spec
pointers and the round-12 repointing that rotted within two dispatches. Line numbers are
therefore **replaced by grep anchors**: a short verbatim string from the sentence carrying
the claim. Each anchor was machine-checked to occur **exactly once** in `main.qmd` and to
lie **within one line**, so it survives reflow, insertion and section reordering.

Resolve any anchor to a current line number with:

```bash
grep -n -F 'ANCHOR' paper/qmd/main.qmd
```

Resolve all of them at once, and re-verify uniqueness, with:

```bash
grep -o -P "(?<=^\| )[^|]*(?= \|)" quality_reports/claim_source_map_panel-npiv-discrete.md
```

Line numbers appear in the **Source** columns only, where they point into the theory
corpus. That corpus is frozen and checksummed; `main.qmd` is not.

## Derived numbers

One row above is not transcribed from the corpus. It is an arithmetic evaluation of a
display the paper itself prints, so it is recorded in closed form and is checkable by hand
without running anything. From `rem:rootnscope`(5) and `cor:ratefloor`(a):

$$\alpha=\frac{r}{2r+d_Z},\qquad \kappa=\frac{2\mu}{2\mu+1},\qquad
\beta=2\kappa\alpha-\tfrac12,\qquad n^\ast=\exp\Big\{\frac{2\kappa}{\beta}\Big\}.$$

| $(r,d_Z,\mu)$ | $\alpha$ | $\kappa$ | $\kappa\alpha$ | $\beta$ | $2\kappa/\beta$ | $n^\ast$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $(5,1,2)$ | $\tfrac5{11}$ | $\tfrac45$ | $\tfrac4{11}$ | $\tfrac5{22}$ | $\tfrac{176}{25}$ | $e^{176/25}\approx1{,}141$ |
| $(5,1,4)$ | $\tfrac5{11}$ | $\tfrac89$ | $\tfrac{40}{99}$ | $\tfrac{61}{198}$ | $\tfrac{352}{61}$ | $e^{352/61}\approx321$ |
| $(12,1,10)$ | $\tfrac{12}{25}$ | $\tfrac{20}{21}$ | $\tfrac{16}{35}$ | $\tfrac{29}{70}$ | $\tfrac{400}{87}$ | $e^{400/87}\approx99$ |

All three satisfy $\kappa\alpha>\tfrac14$, so all three sit **inside** `eq:frontier` and
every hypothesis of `thm:rootn` is available at them. The manuscript rounds to
$1{,}140$, $320$ and $99$.

## Stale upstream artifact identified in this round

`rem:rootnscope`(5)'s **headline** reads "It is an asymptotic statement whose asymptotics
do not bind at any sample size a user will run" (`results.tex` L5181). The **body** of the
same item is correctly scoped — it says the threshold "is astronomically large **near the
frontier**" (L5194). The headline over-generalises, and the table above refutes it from the
corpus's own $n^\ast$ display: at $(5,1,4)$ the turn is at $n\approx321$.

The manuscript no longer carries the over-general form. **The corpus headline is now the
stale artifact.** Correcting it is a theory-corpus edit and is out of the writer's scope;
this row exists so the divergence is on the record rather than discovered later as a
contradiction between §4 and the printed remark.
